                    ### Question
                    A 58-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with complaints of chest pain and palpitations. A thorough past medical history reveals a diagnosis of rheumatic fever during childhood. Echocardiography is conducted and shows enlargement of the left atrium and narrowing of the mitral valve opening. Which of the following should the physician expect , to hear on cardiac auscultation?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Mid-systolic click
opb. Holosystolic murmur that radiates to the axilla
opc. Opening snap following the aortic component of the S2 heart sound
opd. Continuous, machine-like murmur
ope. High-pitched, blowing decrescendo murmur in early diastole

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Rheumatic fever in childhood can lead to mitral valve damage and subsequent mitral stenosis, resulting in narrowing of the mitral valve opening on echocardiography. Turbulent blood flow across the stenotic valve generates a murmur. The physician should expect a high-pitched, blowing decrescendo murmur in early diastole on cardiac auscultation.
